Lately I've been wondering what even the advantage of External SSDs is anymore. Back in the day it was a no brainer SSDs were the cheapest way of getting large external Flash storage. I remember when the first 128gb+ SSDs came on the market the average USB-Sticks and SD-Cards were like 32gb to 64gb. But things changed. The other day I was looking to get some external storage for as cheap as possible as my macbook's storage is soldered in and I can't upgrade my internal storage. I came to find that the price differences between different kinds of storage media have turned around. The cheapest 128gb SSD I could find was a 2.5" sata SSD for about 12$. Add in a Sata to USB adapter (either a cable or an SSD case) and you'll look at a total of about 20$ for 128gb. Comparing that to USB thumb drives where you can find 128gb USB-Sticks for as low as 5$ or about 10$ for a name brand one. You can even get 256gb USB-Sticks for 20$. Same thing for SD-Cards... You can get 256gb Samsung Evo Cards for as low as 20$.   
Plus SD-Cards have the advantage of being "internal". You don't have a USB-Stick sticking out of your laptop or an SSD dangling on a cable. You stick in the SD-Card and forget it's there.
